title: vsftpd 2.3.4 smiley-face backdoor (root RCE)
why: This exact build shipped from a compromised mirror with a backdoor: a username ending in ':)' opens a root shell on 6200/tcp. Trivial, reliable root.

title: ProFTPD 1.3.5 mod_copy unauthenticated file copy -> RCE
why: mod_copy exposes SITE CPFR/CPTO without auth; copy a PHP payload into the webroot for code execution.

title: OpenSSH < 7.7 username enumeration
why: Pre-7.7 sshd reveals whether a username exists via timing/response differences — build a valid user list for spraying.

title: libssh 0.6-0.8 authentication bypass
why: Server-side libssh accepts a client-sent SSH2_MSG_USERAUTH_SUCCESS, letting you skip authentication entirely.

title: Apache httpd 2.4.49 path traversal + RCE
why: Path normalization flaw allows ../ traversal; with mod_cgi enabled it becomes remote code execution.

title: Apache httpd 2.4.50 path traversal + RCE (41773 bypass)
why: The 2.4.49 fix was incomplete; double-encoding restores traversal and RCE via mod_cgi.

title: Samba 3.5.0-4.6.4 is_known_pipename() RCE (SambaCry)
why: A writable share lets you load a malicious .so via a crafted pipe name and execute it as the smbd user.

title: Microsoft IIS 6.0 WebDAV ScStoragePathFromUrl RCE
why: WebDAV PROPFIND buffer overflow on IIS 6.0 gives remote code execution against this end-of-life server.

title: Apache Tomcat AJP connector exposed (Ghostcat)
why: An exposed AJP/1.3 connector (8009) lets you read files under the webapp (e.g. WEB-INF/web.config) and, if uploads exist, achieve RCE.

title: Elasticsearch < 1.4.3 Groovy sandbox bypass RCE
why: The Groovy scripting sandbox can be escaped through the _search API to run OS commands unauthenticated.

title: Redis server reachable — check for no-auth RCE
why: If Redis has no requirepass, you can write an SSH key, cron job, or module for code execution. pwnscout's verify stage checks auth automatically.
next_step: redis-cli -h {ip} -p {port} info server ; redis-cli -h {ip} -p {port} config get dir

title: SMTP service — test for open relay and user enumeration
why: SMTP often leaks valid users via VRFY/EXPN/RCPT and may relay mail. Useful for phishing pretext and user lists.

title: Exim 4.87-4.91 RCE (The Return of the WIZard)
why: A crafted recipient address triggers command execution as root in this Exim range.

title: MySQL/MariaDB exposed to network
why: A network-reachable MySQL invites credential attacks (root with blank/weak password is common on lab and CTF boxes).
next_step: mysql -h {ip} -P {port} -u root --password='' -e 'show databases;' ; hydra -l root -P rockyou.txt {ip} mysql

title: Microsoft SQL Server exposed (1433)
why: MSSQL with sa and a weak password enables xp_cmdshell code execution. Impacket's mssqlclient makes this fast.

title: SMB (445) open — check MS17-010 / SMBv1
why: If SMBv1 is enabled this box may be EternalBlue-vulnerable — one of the most reliable Windows RCEs. Confirm before firing.

title: RDP (3389) open — check BlueKeep / NLA
why: Legacy Windows without NLA may be BlueKeep-vulnerable (pre-auth RCE) and is always a credential-spray target.

title: VNC service exposed — test for no/weak auth
why: VNC frequently has no password or a trivially crackable one, granting instant interactive desktop access.

title: SNMP (161/udp) — try public/private community strings
why: Default community strings dump processes, users, routes, and sometimes credentials in enterprise gear.

title: NFS (2049) exposed — enumerate exports
why: World-readable/writable exports (and no_root_squash) leak files or enable privilege escalation via crafted SUID binaries.

title: Memcached exposed (11211) — no auth by design
why: Memcached has no auth; dump keys for cached sessions/tokens, and it is abusable for UDP amplification.

title: rpcbind/portmapper (111) exposed
why: Enumerating RPC programs reveals NFS, NIS and other services (and their dynamic ports) to attack next.

title: LDAP (389) exposed — try anonymous bind
why: Anonymous LDAP bind on a Domain Controller dumps users, groups and sometimes description-field passwords.
next_step: ldapsearch -x -H ldap://{ip} -s base namingcontexts ; ldapsearch -x -H ldap://{ip} -b 'DC=domain,DC=com'

title: Telnet (23) exposed — cleartext + default creds
why: Telnet sends credentials in cleartext and is usually IoT/network gear with vendor default logins.

title: Docker Engine API exposed (2375) — instant host RCE
why: An unauthenticated Docker API lets you launch a container mounting the host filesystem — trivial full host compromise.
next_step: docker -H tcp://{ip}:2375 ps ; docker -H tcp://{ip}:2375 run -v /:/mnt --rm -it alpine chroot /mnt sh
